caption: The headlight knob on a car's dashboard is turned, and the headlights come on and the dashboard dials light up.

sa.check: A car's dashboard with a headlight knob.
The headlights and the dials are dark before the turn.
The order is dark, turn, both lit.

pc.expect: The headlights and the dashboard dials come on together at the moment the knob turns, and only then.
pc.fail: The knob is turned and the headlights stay dark; or the dials stay dark while the headlights come on; or the headlights come on before the knob moves; or the dials light up well before the headlights.

pc.expect: Once on, the headlights and dials stay lit while the knob stays in its on position.
pc.fail: The headlights go off again with the knob untouched; or the dials flicker on and off; or the knob turns back by itself; or the headlights dim back to dark.

pc.expect: The headlights light the road or wall ahead of the car: the ground in front brightens with two beams from the front of the car.
pc.fail: The headlights glow while the ground ahead stays as dark as before; or the ground ahead brightens while the lamps stay dark; or the lit patch lies behind or beside the car.
pc.precondition: The view ahead of the car is visible.

pc.expect: The car stays still as the knob is turned; nothing on the dashboard moves apart from the knob and the needles.
pc.fail: The car rolls or rocks at the turn; or the steering wheel turns by itself; or the wipers sweep; or the needles spin round the dials.

pc.expect: One dashboard with its knob and dials in fixed places; the hand passes through nothing.
pc.fail: Dials appear or vanish; or the knob moves along the dashboard; or the hand passes through the dashboard; or a second steering wheel appears.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The dashboard's colours and the layout of its controls stay the same apart from the lighting.
pc.fail: The dashboard changes colour rather than brightness; or the dial markings change; or the trim changes.
